subject: URGENT: Medisys production 429s & latency spikes — possible quota/burst policy issue
messages:
From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@medisys.ai>
To: evelyn.hart@redwood.com
Cc: support@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 18 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production: sudden 429s and latency spikes (p95 > 3s)

Evelyn —

We're seeing a production incident starting ~08:45 PT. Traffic is getting a surge of 429s and P95 latency has jumped above 3s for our inference routes. Throughput is artificially capped at roughly half of what we expect based on our committed capacity. Attached is a 200-line tail of our client-side errors plus a Grafana snapshot (prod-traffic-chart.png).

Symptoms: 
- ~20% of requests returning 429s (token-level).
- Sustained p95 latency ~3–4s (was ~300–400ms baseline).
- Request throughput plateaued despite backlog of queued jobs.

We suspect a rate/quotas change or burst-window adjustment on your side; this started immediately after an automated policy rollout we were told would be non-disruptive. Please confirm if any account-level rate/quotas or burst policies were changed for RDW-7452. We need either a rollback or an immediate override while we triage.

This is impacting our live customers and scheduled jobs. Please escalate — we need a rollback or a temporary capacity bump now.

Jordan
Jordan Lee
Head of Engineering, Medisys
jordan.lee@medisys.ai
+1 415 555 0123

Attachments: medisys_error_log_tail.txt, prod-traffic-chart.png

Jordan — thank you for the heads up and for the attachments. I'm escalating this immediately.

Immediate actions I'm starting now: 
- Opening an incident with Eng (cc: Vivek) and Ops to check recent policy rollouts for RDW-7452.
- Requesting an emergency burst/quota override while we investigate.
- I'll share a timeline and keep you updated every 30 minutes until resolved.

Vivek — can you triage whether a safety-valve or burst-window change landed on this account around 08:40 PT? If it's a config rollback, please include the exact rollback command so Ops can apply it.

Jordan — would you also forward any proxy logs showing the 429 headers (x-rate-limit-*) if available; that will speed diagnosis.

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: evelyn.hart@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Cc: neha.kapoor@redwood.com, jordan.lee@medisys.ai
Date: Tue, 18 May 2026 09:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production: sudden 429s and latency spikes (p95 > 3s)

Quick triage notes (initial):
- I can reproduce the pattern in our telemetry: an account-level policy evaluation triggered a new "burst_window_v2" guard at 08:39 PT. The guard reduces short-term burst allowance for accounts without recent usage signals.
- For RDW-7452 the burst allowance dropped ~55% compared to prior window; effective QPS quota stayed the same but the burst budget consumption is much lower which explains the throughput plateau and client-side 429s.
- We're seeing a simultaneous increase in per-request CPU on the serving workers (likely longer KV-cache cold starts caused by higher backpressure).

Immediate mitigation plan (ETA ~30–45m):
1) Roll back the burst_window_v2 toggle for RDW-7452 (Ops can run rollback_patch.diff).
2) Apply a temporary manual burst override (+100% burst tokens) for next 2 hours while we monitor.
3) If rollback proceeds, we'll also clear a small KV-cache ripple on a subset of pods to reduce p95 latency.

I'll take lead on 1–2. Ops: please standby for the rollback command — I will need the green light to run it from an authorized approver.

Vivek Kulkarni
Sr. Engineering Manager, Production Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com

Attachments: rollback_patch.diff (text/x-diff)

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: evelyn.hart@redwood.com, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com
Cc: neha.kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 18 May 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: FWD: Executive notification — Medisys production impact

Evelyn / Vivek —

Drafting an executive note for leadership and Finance since this may require a one-time capacity credit and a formal incident report. Short version for execs: Medisys (RDW-7452) experienced enforced request throttling after an account-level burst-window guard was rolled out; Engineering is rolling back and applying a temporary override. Impact: customer-facing 429s, elevated p95 latency for ~45–90 minutes, material effect on scheduled batch jobs.

Asks: 
- Approve a one-time capacity override + commit to review policy rollout gating (I recommend a brief pause on further auto-rollouts until we have a postmortem).
- Approve a goodwill credit up to 10% of May invoice if incident confirmed to be from our policy change.

I'll send the exec note once you confirm language; if you want I can loop Legal/Finance for the credit approval.

Laura Bennett
Director, Strategic Accounts
laura.bennett@redwood.com

From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@medisys.ai>

Cc: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 19 May 2026 02:45:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Production: sudden 429s and latency spikes (p95 > 3s)

Evelyn / team — thank you. We saw the 429s drop to near-zero within ~12 minutes of the rollback and throughput recovered to expected levels. P95 latency is still elevated (~850ms) but much improved from the peak; looks like the KV-cache ripple is still settling.

We'll keep monitoring on our side and will upload a full client-side trace if anything else pops up. For next steps, we'd like a short incident write-up and the timeline of the rollout (who approved auto-rollout for burst_window_v2) so we can review internal expectations.

Appreciate the quick response.

Jordan
